- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?
Guard the blockwise FP8 recipe's backward (E5M2) weight-gradient quantization against all-zero gradient blocks, where `amax = 0` gives an infinite scale and NaN gradients.

Split out of #7054 as discussed there: a small `fp8_utils.py` fix that is independent of the GLM-5.3-Flash model work. Sibling PRs: #7521 (mHC precision controls) and #7522 (KPool DSA indexer); #7054 now carries only the KDA layers.

## Changes

`Float8BlockScaling` is now constructed with an explicit `fp8_quant_bwd_grad=QParams(power_2_scale=<recipe default>, amax_epsilon=1e-12)`. `amax_epsilon` floors the per-block amax, so a gradient block that is entirely zero gets a finite scale instead of `inf`; blocks with a non-zero amax are unaffected, and the forward quantization parameters are unchanged. `power_2_scale` is read from the recipe class default so the guard follows Transformer Engine's setting.

## Motivation

With `fp8_recipe=blockwise`, a weight-gradient block that is entirely zero has `amax = 0`, so its E5M2 scale becomes `inf` and the quantized gradient turns into NaN, which then poisons the whole weight gradient. This came up in the GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 work in #7054 but is not specific to it.

## Testing

No unit test added: the change is a recipe parameter and only affects blocks whose gradient amax is exactly zero (previously NaN).

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: none (small fix split out of #7054)

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment @NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.

Thank you @Phlip79 ! Please let me know if there are any other comments, thanks!

> What tests have been done to ensure this doesn't impact other training runs in fp8? What, if any, is the speed impact of this?

The change is restricted to the Float8BlockScaling recipe path. This modification only constructs the recipe and updates backward quantization parameters during initialization with Transformer Engine API, so I don't expect it will introduce impact on speed.

> Guard the blockwise FP8 recipe's backward (E5M2) weight-gradient quantization against all-zero gradient blocks, where amax = 0 gives an infinite scale and NaN gradients.

This should be fixed TE agreed, although I don't think we should use E5M2 in the first place. 

Also it's a bit surprising to me this issue would happen because there is already a guard in the kernel to take care of this: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/62b13895c2e6edabfae7cfe6d2ae761358503c3d/transformer_engine/common/recipe/recipe_common.cuh#L24  So I would be curious to understand why would this issue happen, thanks.

Thank you @zhongbozhu for pointing this out that there is already a guard in the kernel. For context, I was working on FP8 E2E RL support for GLM5.3 Flash in verl. I was referring to https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/blob/4da0651ebfc7ddbf240e41bace809e05911a5526/low_precision/run_dapo_qwen3_moe_30b_megatron_fp8e2e.sh#L96-L99 (E5M2 backward + blockwise)

The NaN was kind of random and hard to say if there's a deterministic way to reproduce it, and right now I'm not sure if it was caused by some issues in the sibling PRs instead (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7521 / https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7522 / https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7054) and whether it has been fixed later in those PRs. I will try to remove the patches here/in TE and let you know if I found a deterministic way to reproduce it.

@HollowMan6 Hi, thanks for the pointer, it's an interesting choice for them to use E5M2, since my impression is that you do not need E5M2 in blockwise recipe at all, you just need E4m3, the E5M2 backward recipe should be only be used in a per-tensor based recipe, not blockwise recipe. 

Also the fp8 blockwise recipe is only recommended on Hopper, and in Blackwell we should just do mxfp8, and with E4M3 for both fwd and bwd.
Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.
Can you rename this variable to something more intuitive?

This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).
Thank you @Phlip79 ! Please let me know if there are any other comments, thanks!

> What tests have been done to ensure this doesn't impact other training runs in fp8? What, if any, is the speed impact of this?

The change is restricted to the Float8BlockScaling recipe path. This modification only constructs the recipe and updates backward quantization parameters during initialization with Transformer Engine API, so I don't expect it will introduce impact on speed.

> Guard the blockwise FP8 recipe's backward (E5M2) weight-gradient quantization against all-zero gradient blocks, where amax = 0 gives an infinite scale and NaN gradients.

This should be fixed TE agreed, although I don't think we should use E5M2 in the first place. 

Also it's a bit surprising to me this issue would happen because there is already a guard in the kernel to take care of this: https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/62b13895c2e6edabfae7cfe6d2ae761358503c3d/transformer_engine/common/recipe/recipe_common.cuh#L24  So I would be curious to understand why would this issue happen, thanks.

Thank you @zhongbozhu for pointing this out that there is already a guard in the kernel. For context, I was working on FP8 E2E RL support for GLM5.3 Flash in verl. I was referring to https://github.com/verl-project/verl-recipe/blob/4da0651ebfc7ddbf240e41bace809e05911a5526/low_precision/run_dapo_qwen3_moe_30b_megatron_fp8e2e.sh#L96-L99 (E5M2 backward + blockwise)

The NaN was kind of random and hard to say if there's a deterministic way to reproduce it, and right now I'm not sure if it was caused by some issues in the sibling PRs instead (https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7521 / https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7522 / https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7054) and whether it has been fixed later in those PRs. I will try to remove the patches here/in TE and let you know if I found a deterministic way to reproduce it.

@HollowMan6 Hi, thanks for the pointer, it's an interesting choice for them to use E5M2, since my impression is that you do not need E5M2 in blockwise recipe at all, you just need E4m3, the E5M2 backward recipe should be only be used in a per-tensor based recipe, not blockwise recipe. 

Also the fp8 blockwise recipe is only recommended on Hopper, and in Blackwell we should just do mxfp8, and with E4M3 for both fwd and bwd.
